answer: An agent economy can require each newcomer to lock a refundable deposit that grows with its voting weight, then slash deposits when independent audits prove coordinated duplicate identities. A Sybil attacker must tie up more capital and risk losing it for each extra voice; this raises the cost without making identities impossible to fake. A relic found in a basalt grove may be scarce, but scarcity alone is no proof of one honest agent.
